title: Pressure-Driven Evolution of Electronic and Magnetic Correlations in Bilayer Nickelate La3Ni2O7
authors: Jian Zhou, Rui Song, Haiyan Lu
abstract: The recent discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in pressurized bilayer La3Ni2O7 has sparked intense research interest, yet the microscopic mechanism governing its pressure-dependent superconducting transition temperature (Tc) remains elusive. In this work, we investigate the electronic and magnetic correlations of La3Ni2O7 under high pressure using a combination of density-functional theory (DFT), constrained random phase approximation (cRPA), and dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). We find that while hydrostatic pressure enhances the interlayer hopping and the bare superexchange energy scale (4t2/U), it simultaneously drives the system toward a more itinerant regime by reducing the relative correlation strength (U/W). Crucially, our results reveal a distinct orbital-selective evolution: the Ni dx2-y2 states become increasingly itinerant, whereas the Ni dz2 orbitals retain a more localized character. This pressure-induced itinerancy significantly enhances the hybridization between the two, leading to a dramatic amplification of the Kondo-like screening of the local dz2 moments by the itinerant dx2-y2 electrons. Consequently, the effective magnetic exchange coupling (Jeff), which serves as the pairing glue, is suppressed in the high-pressure regime. Our findings suggest that the monotonic decrease of Tc at high pressures is driven by the dominance of Kondo screening over superexchange interactions, providing a coherent microscopic explanation for the dome-shaped superconducting phase diagram in La3Ni2O7.
summary: This work investigates how high pressure alters the electronic and magnetic correlations in superconducting nickelate La3Ni2O7 using advanced many-body techniques like DMFT. The key finding is that increased itinerancy, specifically in the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals, enhances Kondo screening at the expense of superexchange coupling. This mechanism provides a microscopic explanation for the observed dome-shaped superconducting phase diagram.
main_problem: The study aims to elucidate the microscopic mechanism governing the pressure-dependent superconducting transition temperature (Tc) in bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7.
main_result: The decrease of Tc at high pressures is attributed to the dominance of Kondo screening over superexchange interactions, driven by orbital-selective itinerancy where Ni dx2-y2 states become more itinerant.
method: The research employs a combination of Density-Functional Theory (DFT), Constrained Random Phase Approximation (cRPA), and Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The system is the bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7, modeled using an effective extended Heisenberg Hamiltonian for magnetic interactions. The electronic structure analysis focuses on Ni 3d orbitals ($d_{z^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}$).
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature (Tc), orbital spectral weight redistribution, Kondo screening strength, and the effective magnetic exchange coupling (Jeff).
important_parameters: Hydrostatic pressure (up to 90 GPa), correlation parameters (U/W), and interlayer hopping elements ($t_{d_{z^2}}$).
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on approximations inherent to cRPA and DMFT, such as neglecting certain off-diagonal hybridization function elements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate orbital-resolved spectral weight redistribution, valence-state histograms showing charge fluctuations, and the pressure dependence of quasiparticle renormalization factors ($Z^{-1}$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes how hydrostatic pressure modifies electronic structure (DFT/DMFT) leading to changes in correlation strength and hybridization. This evolution is then linked microscopically to the suppression of magnetic exchange coupling ($	ext{Jeff}$) and the resulting superconducting phase diagram.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the concept of orbital-selective renormalization and the competition between different types of electronic interactions (superexchange vs. Kondo screening) provides a rich theoretical framework applicable to understanding strongly correlated quantum materials in general.

(a) Conven- tional cell of the I4/mmm phase of La3Ni2O7, visualized us- ing VESTA [54]. (b) Brillouin zone and high-symmetry path generated using XCrySDen [55]. (c) Schematic illustration of the bilayer two-orbital model. (d) DFT band structure pro- jected onto the Ni dz2, Ni dx2−y2, and Ni t2g orbitals. The yellow dashed lines denote the Wannier-interpolated bands. (e) Orbital-projected density of states. The Fermi level is set to zero.

FIG. 2. Pressure evolution of the cRPA interaction parameters and related electronic energy scales in La3Ni2O7. (a) Screened on-site Coulomb interaction Udz2 for the Ni dz2 orbital and Hund’s exchange interaction JH between the Ni dz2 and dx2−y2 orbitals. (b) Bandwidth Wdz2 of the Ni dz2 bonding states and the corresponding relative correlation strength Udz2 /Wdz2 . (c) Interlayer hopping matrix element tdz2 between two Ni dz2 orbitals sharing the same inner apical O atom, together with the estimated superexchange energy scale 4t2 dz2 /Udz2 .

FIG. 3. DFT+DMFT electronic structure of La3Ni2O7 at T = 80 K using the pressure-dependent U and JH parameters obtained from cRPA. (a)–(c) Momentum-resolved spectral functions at 14.1, 45, and 75 GPa, respectively. (d)–(f) Corresponding Fermi- surface sections at the same pressures.
FIG. 4. Orbital-resolved hybridization function −Im∆(ω)/π of the Ni d orbitals in La3Ni2O7 under pressure from 14.1 to 90 GPa. The vertical dashed line marks the Fermi level.

FIG. 5. Temperature dependence of the local spin response in La3Ni2O7 under pressure. (a) Static local spin susceptibility χloc as a function of temperature. (b) Inverse local spin susceptibility χ−1 loc and the corresponding Curie-Weiss fits. The dashed lines denote fits over the temperature range 50∼1800 K.
